alt.en: A printed journal page: the running head "The Ritual of the Seder and the Agada. 561", three lines of English ending "It may fitly form the pendant to this note", ten lines of unpointed Hebrew type with a few letters marked above, and the signature "David Kaufmann."
alt.es: Una página impresa de revista: el encabezado "The Ritual of the Seder and the Agada. 561", tres líneas en inglés que terminan con "It may fitly form the pendant to this note", diez líneas de letra hebrea sin vocales, con unas pocas letras marcadas por arriba, y la firma "David Kaufmann."

caption.en: Jacob ben Judah of London's text of Ki Lo Na'eh, from his book of Jewish law of 1287, as David Kaufmann printed it in 1892; he called it the hymn's original form, with the added lines in which, he wrote, Jacob worked in his own name.
caption.es: El texto de Ki Lo Na'eh de Jacob ben Judah de Londres, de su libro de ley judía de 1287, tal como lo imprimió David Kaufmann en 1892; él lo llamó la forma original del himno, con los versos añadidos en los que, según escribió, Jacob puso su propio nombre.

source: David Kaufmann, "The Ritual of the Seder and the Agada of the English Jews before the Expulsion", The Jewish Quarterly Review, vol. 4 (July 1892), p. 561, all but the blank foot of the page
library: JSTOR Early Journal Content (copy hosted by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive jstor-1450252, image n12; JSTOR stable 10.2307/1450252
licenceEvidence: Published 1892 (The Jewish Quarterly Review, vol. 4); David Kaufmann died 1899; the Hebrew is a 13th-century anonymous text. In JSTOR's Early Journal Content collection on the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/jstor_ejc), "journal materials published prior to 1923 in the United States and prior to 1870 elsewhere" (see rights.md).
credit: JSTOR Early Journal Content, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A stained page of large, bold Hebrew type with vowel points: stanza after stanza in big letters, each followed by a few words in smaller type.
alt.es: Una página manchada de letra hebrea grande y gruesa con signos vocálicos: estrofa tras estrofa en letras grandes, cada una seguida de unas pocas palabras en letra más pequeña.

caption.en: Ki Lo Na'eh in an Ashkenazi Haggadah printed at Prague in 1526: its second to sixth stanzas in large type, each answer cut short after "lecha ulecha" and "ki lo naeh".
caption.es: Ki Lo Na'eh en una Hagadá asquenazí impresa en Praga en 1526: de la segunda a la sexta estrofa en letra grande, con cada respuesta abreviada tras "lecha ulecha" y "ki lo naeh".

source: Haggadah shel Pesach (Prague Haggadah), Prague, Tevet 5287 (1526 to 1527), the middle page of Ki Lo Na'eh, cropped below the first answer
library: National Library of Israel (digital edition; copy hosted by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive PragueHaggadah1526, image n78; NLI digital object IE34061667 (from the IA description's link)
licenceEvidence: Item page https://archive.org/details/PragueHaggadah1526 shows "Public Domain Mark 1.0" (licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Printed in Prague in 1526/27 by Gershom and Gronem ben Solomon ha-Kohen, who died in the 16th century; the hymn is anonymous and older. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: National Library of Israel, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Four lines of printed music headed "KI LO NA'EH" and "Andante": a melody in 3/4 with one flat and English words under the notes, "'Tis seemly God alone to praise:", then eight short lines stacked at each change of words, from "Awe by His throne is;" to "Vig-or His throne is;" and from "Blest He alone is:" to "Wise He alone is:", ending "O Lord, the King-dom Thine own is."
alt.es: Cuatro líneas de música impresa con el título "KI LO NA'EH" y la indicación "Andante": una melodía en 3/4 con un bemol y letra en inglés bajo las notas, "'Tis seemly God alone to praise:", luego ocho líneas cortas apiladas en cada cambio de palabras, de "Awe by His throne is;" a "Vig-or His throne is;" y de "Blest He alone is:" a "Wise He alone is:", y al final "O Lord, the King-dom Thine own is."

caption.en: The tune Rittangel printed at Königsberg in 1644, which the Jewish Encyclopedia called the most alluring of the hymn's airs, as the encyclopedia reprinted it in modern notation in 1904, with an English paraphrase.
caption.es: La melodía que Rittangel imprimió en Königsberg en 1644, que la Jewish Encyclopedia llamó la más atractiva de las del himno, tal como la enciclopedia la reimprimió en notación moderna en 1904, con una paráfrasis en inglés.

source: Cyrus Adler and Francis L. Cohen, "Ki Lo Na'eh", The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 7 (New York: Funk and Wagnalls, 1904), p. 493, the music example; scanned from an undated facsimile reprint by Ktav Publishing House, New York
library: University of California Libraries (UCLA, SRLF; digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: IA metadata https://archive.org/metadata/jewishencycloped07sing: "possible-copyright-status": "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT", "no visible notice of copyright; exact publication date unknown". The scanned copy is an undated Ktav Publishing House facsimile reprint of the 1904 volume (title page), which adds no new authorship. The page was first published in New York in 1904; the article is signed A. (Cyrus Adler, died 1940) and F. L. C. (Francis Lyon Cohen, died 1934); the 1644 tune is far older (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "Ki Lo Noeh", "CHORUS. Andante con moto" and "Traditional": the chorus "Ki lo no-eh Ki lo yo-eh.", then a line marked SOLO with three verses, "Ad-dir bim'-lu-cho", "Ko-dosh bim'-lu-cho" and "Tak-kif bim'-lu-cho", and a CHORUS beginning "l'-cho u-l'-cho", each line over a piano part.
alt.es: Una página impresa de música con el título "Ki Lo Noeh", las indicaciones "CHORUS. Andante con moto" y "Traditional": el coro "Ki lo no-eh Ki lo yo-eh.", luego una línea marcada SOLO con tres estrofas, "Ad-dir bim'-lu-cho", "Ko-dosh bim'-lu-cho" y "Tak-kif bim'-lu-cho", y un CHORUS que empieza "l'-cho u-l'-cho", cada línea sobre una parte de piano.

caption.en: "Ki Lo Noeh" on page 84 of the revised Union Haggadah (1923), marked Traditional, with its verses for a solo voice and its answer for the chorus: the first of the two pages our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: "Ki Lo Noeh" en la página 84 de la Union Haggadah revisada (1923), marcada Traditional, con las estrofas para una voz solista y la respuesta para el coro: la primera de las dos páginas de las que sale nuestro arreglo.

source: Central Conference of American Rabbis, The Union Haggadah: Home Service for the Passover, revised edition (1923), p. 84, "Ki Lo Noeh", without the page number
library: University of Florida, George A. Smathers Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Item page https://archive.org/details/unionhaggadahhom00unse: "Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright". Published in the US in 1923, so its US term ended at the end of 2018; the setting names no arranger (the 1908 edition's Passover music was "edited by the Society of American Cantors"), so 70 years from publication in the EU and Israel (see rights.md).
credit: University of Florida, George A. Smathers Libraries, via the Internet Archive
